title: The Heart in Winter: The Real Butte That Changed the Senate
description:
Steven Spielberg's next film, in the news this week, is The Heart in Winter, a western set in Butte, Montana, in 1891. The real Butte sat on "the Richest Hill on Earth", and the copper fight under it ended in a Senate bribery scandal that helped change how Americans elect their senators.
🚶 Visiting San Diego? Explore its history on a guided tour with Fable: https://fablehospitality.com

Every frame is drawn with code. No stock footage, no AI video.

1:00 How Butte changed the Senate

Note: Facts follow the U.S. Senate Historical Office ("The Election Case of William A. Clark of Montana", 1900), Western Mining History, the Mining History Association, the Copper Development Association, and Montana Historical Society material. Butte's mines passed Lake Superior's as the top US copper source by 1887; by 1896 the district produced about 26% of the world's copper (Mining History Association), and from about 1905 to 1917 between a quarter and a third (Western Mining History). Marcus Daly's Anaconda was bought as a silver mine and turned to copper in the early 1880s. In the 1894 vote on Montana's permanent capital, Clark backed Helena against Daly's Anaconda, and Helena won. In 1899 the Montana legislature elected Clark to the US Senate; witnesses before the Senate committee described bribes "ranging from $240 to $100,000", the committee found unanimously that he was "not entitled to his seat", and Clark resigned on May 15, 1900. He was elected again by the 1901 legislature and served until 1907. Twain's words come from his 1907 essay "Senator Clark of Montana" (published in Mark Twain in Eruption, 1940). Historians count the Clark case among the scandals behind the 17th Amendment (ratified 1913), which made senators "elected by the people thereof". The photographs show Butte around 1875-1900, not the novel or the film.

Images (public domain): photographs and portraits from Harry C. Freeman, "A Brief History of Butte, Montana, the World's Greatest Mining Camp" (Chicago, 1900, Internet Archive): Butte looking south from the center of the city; the Anaconda hill ("Richest mining spot on earth"); "Waiting for the stage coach", early Butte; the Nipper mine; a steel gallows frame; portraits of Marcus Daly and William A. Clark. Mark Twain, photograph by Histed (frontispiece of Albert Bigelow Paine, "Mark Twain: A Biography", 1912). Documents drawn in code.
Maps drawn in code from Natural Earth (world-atlas) and US Census (us-atlas) outlines.
